article_title: HEALTH • HOPE • HAPPINESS • ELECTRICITY IN THE SPARTHFIELD CLINICS
brief_extract: Situated in one of the residential areas of the town, it was once a private residence and stands in its own grounds surrounded by trees and well-kept gardens, with a wonderful view of the Lancashire moors. Sparthfield first entered the hospital world in December, 1937, as a Nursing Home founded by Sir Alfred Joseph Law, primarily for the treatment of Parkinson's disease. It was found, however, that structural deficiencies made it unsuitable for the care of patients requiring nursing attention, so the Hospital Management Committee, guided by their medical and other advisers, decided to close the home and use the building for other Health Service purposes, and after a good deal of conversion it was opened in June, 1953, as an Out-Patients' Clinic.
